subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which general's march on London helped bring about the Restoration of the monarchy in 1660?
questions.explain: General George Monck marched from Scotland to London in 1660 and helped engineer the Restoration of Charles II.

questions.q: In which year was Charles I executed?
questions.explain: Charles I was tried and executed in January 1649.

questions.q: In which year did the Great Fire of London occur?
questions.explain: The Great Fire of London destroyed much of the city in September 1666.

questions.q: Which epidemic struck London in 1665?
questions.explain: The Great Plague of 1665 killed a large proportion of London's population.

questions.q: In which year did the English Civil War break out?
questions.explain: The English Civil War between King and Parliament began in 1642.

questions.q: What was the name of Parliament's reorganised, professional army?
questions.explain: The New Model Army, formed in 1645, was Parliament's disciplined, professional fighting force.

questions.q: Which diarist gave a famous eyewitness account of the Great Fire of London in 1666?
questions.explain: Samuel Pepys recorded a vivid eyewitness account of the Great Fire of London in his diary in 1666.

questions.q: In which year did Charles I begin his 'Personal Rule' without Parliament?
questions.explain: Charles I dissolved Parliament in 1629 and ruled without it until 1640, a period called the Personal Rule.

questions.q: Which event in 1637 saw Charles I provoke unrest by imposing a new Prayer Book on Scotland?
questions.explain: Charles's attempt to impose an English-style Prayer Book on Scotland in 1637 sparked resistance leading to the Bishops' Wars.

questions.q: In which year was the monarchy restored with Charles II returning to the throne?
questions.explain: The monarchy was restored in 1660 when Charles II returned to England.

questions.q: What title did Oliver Cromwell take in 1653?
questions.explain: Cromwell became Lord Protector in 1653, ruling during the Protectorate.

questions.q: Which controversial tax, levied without Parliament's consent, caused anger during the Personal Rule?
questions.explain: Ship money, a tax extended to inland counties without Parliament's approval, provoked strong opposition.

questions.q: Which Cromwell campaign of 1649-50 brutally suppressed resistance with sieges at Drogheda and Wexford?
questions.explain: Cromwell's campaign in Ireland in 1649-50 included the notorious storming of Drogheda and Wexford.

questions.q: What was England called during the republican period after Charles I's execution?
questions.explain: After 1649 England was governed as a republic known as the Commonwealth.

questions.q: Charles I was forced to recall Parliament in 1640 mainly because he needed what?
questions.explain: Charles recalled Parliament in 1640 because he urgently needed money to fund war against the Scots.

questions.q: What charge was Charles I found guilty of at his trial in 1649?
options: Treason against the people of England
questions.explain: Charles I was tried and condemned as a tyrant and traitor against the people of England, and executed in January 1649.

questions.q: Which 1644 battle in the north was a major Parliamentarian victory in the Civil War?
questions.explain: The Battle of Marston Moor in 1644 was a decisive Parliamentarian victory in northern England.

questions.q: Which decisive 1645 battle effectively destroyed the King's main field army?
questions.explain: The Battle of Naseby in 1645 saw the New Model Army crush the King's main army, sealing Parliament's victory.

questions.q: What was the central political conflict that led to the English Civil War?
options: The power of the King versus the rights of Parliament
questions.explain: The war arose from the struggle over whether the King or Parliament held ultimate authority.

questions.q: Who was commissioned to rebuild St Paul's Cathedral after the Great Fire of 1666?
questions.explain: Sir Christopher Wren designed and oversaw the rebuilding of St Paul's Cathedral following the Great Fire.

questions.q: Outside which London building was Charles I executed in January 1649?
questions.explain: Charles I was beheaded on a scaffold outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall in January 1649.

questions.q: Who emerged as the leading commander of Parliament's forces and later ruled England?
questions.explain: Oliver Cromwell rose to lead Parliament's forces and later became Lord Protector.
